rows.body: In a Young's double-slit experiment with λ = 500 nm, D = 1 m and d = 1 mm, a thin transparent sheet of thickness 10 μm and refractive index 1.5 is placed in front of one slit. By how many fringes does the pattern shift?
rows.explanation: The shift of the pattern is x = (μ − 1)tD/d = 0.5 × 10 μm × 1 m / 1 mm = 5 mm. The fringe width is β = λD/d = 0.5 mm, so the number of fringes shifted is x/β = (μ − 1)t/λ = 10.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 10 Wave Optics, Sec 10.5 (Young's double-slit experiment)

rows.subject: physics
rows.body: Maxwell introduced displacement current to make Ampère’s law consistent for a capacitor being charged. Displacement current is associated with which quantity?

options.text: The rate of change of electric flux, ε₀ dΦE/dt
The flow of free electrons in the connecting wire
The steady magnetic field produced by a constant current
The rate of change of magnetic monopole density

rows.explanation: Displacement current I_d = ε₀ dΦE/dt is not a flow of charge. It is the changing electric field between capacitor plates, and it produces a magnetic field just as a conduction current does. This correction keeps Ampère’s law consistent with charge conservation.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 8 Electromagnetic Waves, Sec 8.2 (Displacement current)

rows.subject: physics
rows.body: Given μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A and ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² C²/(N·m²), what is the speed of electromagnetic waves in vacuum, from c = 1/√(μ₀ε₀)?
rows.explanation: μ₀ε₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ × 8.85 × 10⁻¹² ≈ 1.11 × 10⁻¹⁷ s²/m². Taking the reciprocal square root gives c ≈ 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s. The speed of light is therefore fixed by the electric and magnetic properties of vacuum.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 8 Electromagnetic Waves, Sec 8.2 to 8.3 (Electromagnetic waves and their speed)

rows.subject: physics
rows.body:
Arrange the following electromagnetic waves in order of increasing wavelength, shortest wavelength first.
(A) Radio waves
(B) Visible light
(C) Gamma rays
(D) Microwaves
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
rows.explanation: Wavelength decreases as frequency increases across the spectrum. Radio waves are the longest, then microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays are the shortest. So increasing wavelength runs gamma rays, visible light, microwaves, radio waves.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 8 Electromagnetic Waves, Sec 8.4 (Electromagnetic spectrum)

rows.subject: physics
rows.body:
Match List-I (electromagnetic wave) with List-II (use).
List-I: (A) Infrared, (B) Ultraviolet, (C) X-rays, (D) Microwaves
List-II: (I) Sterilising water and killing bacteria, (II) Radiographs of bones, (III) Thermal imaging and TV remote controls, (IV) Radar and satellite communication
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
rows.explanation: Infrared is used in thermal imaging and remote controls (III), ultraviolet sterilises water and kills bacteria (I), X-rays produce radiographs of bones (II), and microwaves are used in radar and satellite communication (IV). The correct pairing is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(IV).
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 8 Electromagnetic Waves, Sec 8.4 (Electromagnetic spectrum and uses)

rows.subject: physics
rows.body: An electromagnetic wave travels in the −z direction in vacuum. At an instant, its magnetic field points along +x. Along which direction does its electric field point at that instant?
rows.explanation: In an electromagnetic wave E, B and the direction of propagation are mutually perpendicular, with propagation along E × B. With B along +x and propagation along −z, E must be along +y, since ŷ × x̂ = −ẑ. So the electric field points along +y at that instant.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 8 Electromagnetic Waves, Sec 8.3 (Electromagnetic waves: transverse nature and E, B directions)

rows.subject: physics
rows.body: A microwave of frequency 1.5 GHz travels in vacuum. What is its wavelength? (Take c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s.)
rows.explanation: The wavelength in vacuum is λ = c/f = (3 × 10⁸)/(1.5 × 10⁹) = 0.2 m. All electromagnetic waves travel at c in vacuum, so wavelength and frequency are inversely related.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 8 Electromagnetic Waves, Sec 8.4 (Electromagnetic spectrum)

rows.subject: physics
rows.body: An equilateral prism of refracting angle A = 60° is set at minimum deviation, where the angle of minimum deviation is δm = 30°. What is the refractive index of the prism material?
rows.explanation: At minimum deviation the refractive index is μ = sin((A + δm)/2) / sin(A/2) = sin 45° / sin 30° = 0.707 / 0.5 ≈ 1.41. The prism angle and the minimum deviation together fix the index, so the formula is applied directly.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 9 Ray Optics, Sec 9.6 (Refraction through a prism)

rows.subject: physics
rows.body: What is the approximate critical angle for light travelling from glass (μ = 1.5) to air?
rows.explanation: The critical angle C satisfies sin C = μ_air/μ_glass = 1/1.5 = 2/3. Since sin 42° ≈ 0.67, C ≈ 42°. Light striking the interface at angles larger than C undergoes total internal reflection.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 9 Ray Optics, Sec 9.4 (Total internal reflection)

rows.subject: physics
rows.body: An astronomical telescope in normal adjustment has an objective of focal length 120 cm and an eyepiece of focal length 4 cm. What is its magnifying power?
rows.explanation: In normal adjustment the magnifying power of an astronomical telescope is M = f_o/f_e = 120/4 = 30. The final image is at infinity, and the length of the telescope is then f_o + f_e.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Physics Part II, Ch 9 Ray Optics, Sec 9.7 (Optical instruments: telescope)

rows.subject: physics
rows.body: A sinusoidal alternating current i = I₀ sin ωt flows in a circuit. What is the average value of the current over one half cycle, from t = 0 to t = T/2?
rows.explanation: Over a complete cycle the average of a sine function is zero, but over a half cycle it is not. The half-cycle average is (2/T) ∫₀^(T/2) I₀ sin ωt dt = 2I₀/π ≈ 0.637 I₀. I₀/√2 is the rms value, which is a different quantity.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Physics Part I, Ch 7 Alternating Current, Sec 7.2 (AC voltage applied to a resistor)

rows.body: A 100 μF capacitor is connected to a 50 Hz AC supply. What is its capacitive reactance?
rows.explanation: Capacitive reactance is X_C = 1/(ωC), where ω = 2πf ≈ 314 rad/s. So X_C = 1/(314 × 100 × 10⁻⁶) ≈ 31.8 Ω. Reactance falls as frequency or capacitance increases, and an ideal capacitor dissipates no average power.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Physics Part I, Ch 7 Alternating Current, Sec 7.5 (AC voltage applied to a capacitor)

rows.subject: physics
rows.body: A series LCR circuit has R = 3 Ω, X_L = 8 Ω and X_C = 4 Ω. An rms current of 10 A flows in the circuit. What is the average power dissipated?
rows.explanation: The impedance is Z = √(R² + (X_L − X_C)²) = √(9 + 16) = 5 Ω, so cos φ = R/Z = 0.6. The average power is P = I_rms²R = 100 × 3 = 300 W, which equals V_rms I_rms cos φ = 50 × 10 × 0.6. Reactive components do not dissipate average power.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Physics Part I, Ch 7 Alternating Current, Sec 7.6 and 7.7 (series LCR circuit and power in AC circuits)

rows.subject: physics
rows.body: A series LCR circuit has L = 2 mH and C = 50 μF. What is its resonant frequency?
rows.explanation: Resonance occurs when X_L = X_C, at f₀ = 1/(2π√(LC)). Here LC = 1.0 × 10⁻⁷ s², so √(LC) = 3.16 × 10⁻⁴ s and f₀ ≈ 503 Hz. At resonance the impedance is minimum and the power factor is unity.
tags: ncert:NCERT Class 12 Physics Part I, Ch 7 Alternating Current, Sec 7.6 (LCR series circuit and resonance)

rows.subject: physics
rows.body: An ideal step-up transformer has turns ratio N_p : N_s = 1 : 20 and is connected to a 230 V supply. If the secondary delivers 0.5 A to its load, what is the current in the primary coil?
rows.explanation: For an ideal transformer, V_p I_p = V_s I_s. The secondary voltage is 4600 V, so 230 × I_p = 4600 × 0.5 and I_p = 10 A. A step-up transformer raises voltage and reduces current on the secondary side in the same proportion.
